# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with his heart, requiring regular check-ups to monitor its condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences food textures as a real challenge, making eating a difficult task.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, affecting his muscle tone and overall physical strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone and overall physical strength.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty in noisy environments, becoming frustrated easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), with squint being a possible feature.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to brush his teeth carefully and regularly to maintain proper enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: The vast majority of people with KBG syndrome learn to speak, but speech delay is very common.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, affecting his muscle tone and overall physical strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone and overall physical strength.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, and the patient appears to be a bit behind his peers in terms of overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hip dysplasia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, and the patient appears to be a bit behind his peers in terms of overall development.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for heart valve issues and perform regular check-ups to monitor the condition.
b) Work with a specialist to address feeding difficulties and ensure proper tooth brushing techniques.
c) Monitor growth velocity and refer for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
d) Refer for orthopedic evaluation if asymmetrical hip creases or painful gait are noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures from time to time, requiring close monitoring with a neurologist and adjusting medication as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and they typically respond to the usual antiepileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than average and some palatal abnormalities that the doctors keep an eye on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: About 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away, and she wears glasses to help correct this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has chewing challenges, particularly with harder foods, and needs to eat softer foods and take smaller bites to make mealtime easier.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and they typically respond to the usual antiepileptic treatments.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and they typically respond to the usual antiepileptic treatments.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that the specialists are monitoring, including regular check-ups to ensure everything is progressing as it should.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a recognized feature of KBG syndrome, impacting speech and feeding.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that the specialists are monitoring, including regular check-ups to ensure everything is progressing as it should.
